messages.content: I just moved to Canada last year and I spend about $500 on groceries every month. What's the best card?
Welcome! For groceries, the TD Cash Visa or CIBC Dividend Visa are great picks — 4% on groceries.
I prefer cashback over points, and I don't want any annual fee.
Then TD Cash Visa is your match — $0 annual fee, 4% on groceries and gas.
I'm a student with no credit history, what card should I start with?
Try a student card from Scotiabank or TD.
I commute by bus every day and don't travel much.
Then a flat-rate cashback like Scotiabank Momentum is fine — no need for travel perks.
I make over $150k a year and travel internationally every quarter.
You'd benefit from a premium travel card.
I prefer points I can transfer to airlines.
AMEX Platinum or CIBC Aventura would suit you. Both have transfer partners.
I have two young kids and we spend a lot on groceries and gas.
Family-friendly cards focus on groceries/gas.
Roughly $800 on groceries, $300 on gas every month.
TD Cash Visa Infinite covers both at 3-4%.
I'm a permanent resident with a dog. Looking for an everyday cashback card.
Cashback cards are great for everyday spending.
I don't want any annual fee.
Tangerine Money-Back is a solid $0-fee choice.
I don't want any AMEX cards — too many places don't accept them.
Understood. I'll focus on Visa and Mastercard options.
Show me grocery cards from TD or CIBC.
TD Cash Visa or CIBC Dividend Visa — both great for groceries.
I just got my work permit. My income is around $40k.
Welcome! A starter card is best for now.
What's a good no-fee starter card?
Try CIBC Costco Mastercard or PC Financial — both $0 fee.
I eat out a lot — about $400 a month on dining.
Dining-focused cards earn extra on restaurants.
I also do $500 of online shopping monthly.
AMEX Cobalt covers both: 5x on dining, 1x on online.
I'm a Canadian citizen, $80k income, willing to pay up to $200 annual fee.
Premium cards with $100-200 fees offer great perks.
I'd prefer cashback I can use on anything.
Scotiabank Momentum Visa Infinite — $120 fee, 4% on groceries and gas.
I work from home and rarely commute or travel. Looking for an everyday card.
For everyday spending, a flat-rate cashback card is simple and effective.
How about the Tangerine Money-Back?
Great choice — $0 fee, 2% in three categories you pick. I'd recommend going for it.
